panels.title: Current Work
panels.description: What the worker is doing right now; Phase is the state name, this is the activity inside it.

panels.title: Attempts

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_attempts{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) or (max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_attempts{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range])) unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}))

panels.description: Worker Jobs created so far. Read at the range end first, then over the range only once the Migration is gone: a deleted run keeps what it last reported, while a live one is never answered for by an earlier run that reused its name. Nothing in the range at all reads N/A. No fallback value: the operator records this gauge on every reconcile, so its absence only ever means the Migration is not here.

panels.title: Elapsed

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_completion_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) - max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_start_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) or time() - max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_start_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) or ((max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_completion_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range])) - max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_start_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range]))) unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} * -1)

panels.description: How long the run took once it completed, and how long it has been going while it has not. Read at the range end first, then over the range only once the Migration is gone: a deleted run keeps what it last reported, while a live one is never answered for by an earlier run that reused its name. Nothing in the range at all reads N/A.

panels.title: Completed At

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_completion_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) * 1000 or (max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_completion_time_seconds{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range])) * 1000 unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} * 0)

panels.description: When the run ended. Read at the range end first, then over the range only once the Migration is gone: a deleted run keeps what it last reported, while a live one is never answered for by an earlier run that reused its name. Nothing in the range at all reads N/A.

panels.title: ETA By Size

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, name) (clamp_min(pgcopydb_migration_source_database_size_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} - pgcopydb_migration_target_database_size_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}, 0) / clamp_min(deriv(pgcopydb_migration_target_database_size_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__rate_interval]), 1) / 60) and on (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_phase{namespace="$namespace", name="$name", phase="Cloning"} == 1) or sum by (namespace, name) (-1 * (pgcopydb_migration_phase{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} == 1))

panels.description: Remaining size over how fast the target is currently growing, in whole minutes. Anything under a minute reads as ~1m, because a sub-minute estimate is false precision on a migration. Zero and a day upward both read as Calculating, because both are clamps rather than estimates. Zero means the numerator hit its floor, which is not a finished migration: the target routinely overtakes the source in bytes while index builds and vacuum are still running, since index builds, WAL and page bloat mean the copy never lands byte for byte. A day upward means the denominator hit its floor, because the target stops growing during index builds and deriv falls to zero. deriv and not rate: these are gauges, and rate treats the drop when dropIfExists empties the target as a counter reset. The window follows the dashboard's rate interval rather than a fixed 15m, because a clone can finish inside 15m and a window longer than the run averages the rate down to nothing. Byte-based extrapolation only means anything during Cloning: every later phase has no bytes left to project from, so the panel reads No ETA instead of a clamp that would look like a real number; Phase and Current work, right beside it, already say which phase and what is running.

panels.title: Tables
panels.description: Absent on a plain clone: the operator only samples pgcopydb's catalogs while following, so no value here is not zero progress.

panels.title: Indexes
panels.description: Absent on a plain clone: the operator only samples pgcopydb's catalogs while following, so no value here is not zero progress.

panels.title: Clone Bytes
panels.description: Stays a few percent short of 100 by construction: on-disk size carries headers, padding and free space a COPY stream does not move. Absent on a plain clone: the operator only samples pgcopydb's catalogs while following, so no value here is not zero progress.

panels.title: Schema Verification
panels.description: pgcopydb compare schema: tables, columns, indexes, constraints and sequence values as pgcopydb models them. Deactivated means spec.verification.schema is false, which is also the default, so a migration that never opted in reads Deactivated rather than waiting forever on a check nobody asked for. Pending means the check is requested and has not run yet. A result outranks the spec: switching a check off after it reported a mismatch still reads FAIL.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_verification_check{namespace="$namespace", name="$name", check="schema"}) or (max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_verification_check{namespace="$namespace", name="$name", check="schema"}[$__range])) unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} * -2)

panels.title: Data Verification
panels.description: pgcopydb compare data: per-table row counts and full-table checksums. Deactivated means spec.verification.data is false, which is also the default, so a migration that never opted in reads Deactivated rather than waiting forever on a check nobody asked for. Pending means the check is requested and has not run yet. A result outranks the spec: switching a check off after it reported a mismatch still reads FAIL.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_verification_check{namespace="$namespace", name="$name", check="data"}) or (max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_verification_check{namespace="$namespace", name="$name", check="data"}[$__range])) unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} * -2)

panels.title: Phase Timeline
panels.description: When each phase was first seen in the dashboard range, so a phase entered before the range reads as the range start. The subquery steps at the scrape interval: a phase gauge series only stands until the next scrape marks it stale, so a coarser step walks past short phases entirely. A phase shorter than one scrape leaves no sample at all and cannot appear here; Condition Timeline, beside this, reads the transition times off the CR and does keep those.

panels.title: Condition Timeline
panels.description: When each condition last changed status, straight from its lastTransitionTime, so a phase that lasted a second is still here. Read across the dashboard range rather than at its end: a condition that has since flipped keeps both of its rows, and a Migration that has since been deleted keeps its timeline. Aggregated by condition so an operator restart, which rescrapes the same transition under a new pod label, does not double every row.

panels.title: Database Size
panels.description: Sampled from the worker pod; the series exist only while a worker runs.

panels.title: Copy Throughput
panels.description: rate() over gauges: a shrinking target reads as a counter reset. Clone copy needs the bundled (patched) runner and stays empty otherwise. Target growth is clamped at 0: vacuum reclaims space during Finalizing, and the resulting negative slope is real but meaningless as a byte rate. Clone copy needs no such clamp: it is a monotonic tally from the work-dir catalog that a retry resumes rather than rewinds.

panels.title: LSN Positions
panels.description: Absolute WAL byte positions. Present in follow mode once streaming starts; endpos appears when cutover sets it.

panels.title: WAL Generation
panels.description: How fast the source produces WAL; what the target has to keep up with.

panels.title: Cutover Drain

targets.expr: (max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_endpos_lsn_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}) - max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_replay_lsn_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or ((max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_endpos_lsn_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range])) - max by (namespace, name) (last_over_time(pgcopydb_migration_replay_lsn_bytes{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"}[$__range]))) unless max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"})) or max by (namespace, name) (pgcopydb_migration_info{namespace="$namespace", name="$name"} * -1)

panels.description: Bytes left to replay to reach the cutover endpos; 0 means the drain is done. Read at the range end first, then over the range only once the Migration is gone: a deleted run keeps what it last reported, while a live one is never answered for by an earlier run that reused its name. Nothing in the range at all reads N/A.
